part.text:
Fixed. The bug was in `@babel/generator`: a `FunctionExpression` starting an expression statement (e.g. after the arrow-functions transform turns `(() => {...})().map++;` into `function () {...}().map++;`) was printed without parentheses, producing `SyntaxError: Function statements require a function name`.

The fix in `packages/babel-generator/src/node/parentheses.ts` adds `(isUpdateExpression(parent) && !parent.prefix)` to the `isFirstInContext` walk-up, so `FunctionExpression`/`ClassExpression` at statement-start are wrapped in parens even through call/member/update chains:

- `packages/babel-generator/src/node/parentheses.ts:34` – import `isUpdateExpression`
- `packages/babel-generator/src/node/parentheses.ts:417` – walk-up condition

Verified: the issue repro now outputs valid `(function () { ... })().map(c, v0).map++;`, and the generator, arrow-functions, types, and traverse test suites all pass (553 + 5886 tests).
